  - [amalgamation] a caravan bazaar and a modern transit hub in one carved space - the same facades serve both the camel route and the rail line, and the student decides which era wins each facade.
  - [what-if] Petra is still the regional capital in 2026, the wadi never dried up, and the carved facades are living quarters, not tombs.
- **Design concept thread:** hidden versus revealed space; what a threshold (canyon mouth, gate) does to scale and attention.

### 3. Great Zimbabwe (bank cand. 11)
- **Event:** Great Zimbabwe stone city, 11th-15th c., Shona, Zimbabwe
- **Used in:** W3 P1 list (city in the sky, futuristic renaissance)
- **Regional uniqueness:** (1) Dry-stone masonry - granite blocks fitted without mortar, walls up to about 11 m high in the Great Enclosure (web-verified) - a mass-and-flow subject with almost no surface detail to hide behind. (2) The palette is granite grey, savanna ochre, and dry grass under high, hard light. (3) Craft and symbol: the carved soapstone Great Zimbabwe Bird is the site's iconic artifact and links the name to the bird (bank cand. 11). (4) The site is self-contained - gate, enclosure, pathways - ideal for a single hero render with 3-5 directional studies.
- **Gender angle:** women as potters and traders in the gold and ivory networks - production and exchange, not only court life (bank cand. 11).
- **Class angle:** a trading elite built in stone - the walls themselves are the class marker; gold and ivory trade networks connected the city to Indian Ocean markets (bank cand. 11).
- **Context note:** none flagged.
- **Hooks:**
  - [amalgamation] (bank hook, re-labeled) the "city in the sky" reading - the stone city lifted into the clouds as a renaissance of the dry-stone craft, stone logic kept, gravity dropped.
  - [futuristic] (bank hook) a futuristic renaissance of the stone city - the same enclosures rebuilt with clean geometry and hard light.
  - [what-if] Great Zimbabwe is the world's oldest working financial district, and the Great Enclosure is the exchange floor.
  - [mythological] the soapstone bird takes flight and the city follows it upward - the bird as the reason the city is airborne.
- **Design concept thread:** enclosure and its gate - what massing says about who is inside and who must be admitted; monument versus habitation.

### 4. Tenochtitlan (bank cand. 23)
- **Event:** Aztec capital Tenochtitlan, 14th-16th c., Mesoamerica
- **Used in:** W3 P1 list (city on a new lake, Fifth Sun as engine)
- **Regional uniqueness:** (1) A city on an island in Lake Texcoco, reached by three raised causeways - water as street (web-verified). (2) Chinampa agriculture: cultivated floating beds made the island productive - a distinctive ground-plane texture. (3) Temple architecture: the Great Temple (Templo Mayor) as a stepped pyramid crowning the skyline, with carved stone and stucco. (4) Scale: at its peak Tenochtitlan was among the largest cities in the world, on the order of 200,000 people (web-verified).
- **Gender angle:** women weavers and the merchant class - the bank names women's craft roles and the pochteca merchant class as the commoner spine of the city (bank cand. 23).
- **Class angle:** the calpulli commoner households versus the pipiltin nobility - class is legible in the city's districts, not only in dress (bank cand. 23).
- **Context note:** the Spanish conquest - disease and violence - is the sensitive layer. Suggested framing: frame as the city and its cosmology, not the conquest; the sensitive historical layer is optional context.
- **Hooks:**
  - [amalgamation] (bank hook, re-labeled) a city on a new lake - the Aztec island city re-founded on a new, engineered lake, water-street logic kept.
  - [what-if] the city never fell and simply modernizes - causeways become transit lines, chinampas become hydroponic districts, the temple skyline is preserved.
  - [mythological] (bank hook) the Fifth Sun as a mythological engine at the city's heart - the cosmology made literal as a machine.
- **Design concept thread:** a city organized around water and causeways - how a boundary (lake) becomes the plan; sacred center versus everyday district.

### 5. Samarkand, Timurid era (bank cand. 9)
- **Event:** Samarkand under the Timurid dynasty, 15th c., Central Asia
- **Used in:** W3 P1 list (futuristic oasis of blue tilework)
- **Regional uniqueness:** (1) The Registan ensemble - three madrasas framing a single great square - is a documented masterwork of public-space composition (web-verified). (2) Color is the identity: cobalt and turquoise tilework, with the region's lapis lazuli supply (Badakhshan) feeding the palette (web-verified). (3) The bazaar as mixed-class space - commerce, craft, and court all visible in one street level. (4) High-contrast light: deep blue against sun-bleached plaster.
- **Gender angle:** merchants, artisans, and the women of the souk - the market as the public space where women's economic roles are visible (bank cand. 9).
- **Class angle:** merchants and artisans versus the court; the market as a genuinely mixed-class space is the bank's point (bank cand. 9).
- **Context note:** none flagged.
- **Hooks:**
  - [futuristic] (bank hook) a futuristic oasis of blue tilework - domes and bazaar in motion, the tilework grammar kept into a new era.
  - [amalgamation] the Registan square as a spaceport: the three madrasa facades are kept, but the square's function is departure and arrival of vessels - trade becomes transit.
  - [what-if] the Silk Road never ended and Samarkand is 2026's busiest interchange - the bazaar still runs, just with more lanes.
  - [mythological] (bank hook) the divine king's court of scholars - the madrasa square as the center of a celestial academy.
- **Design concept thread:** a single square holding many functions (study, trade, ceremony); how one dominant color can define an entire built environment.

### 6. House of Wisdom, Baghdad (bank cand. 19)
- **Event:** the House of Wisdom and its translation school, 8th-13th c., Baghdad, Middle East
- **Used in:** W3 P1 list (city as a living archive)
- **Regional uniqueness:** (1) A great round library and translation school at the center of an intellectual culture - the bank's core form (bank cand. 19). (2) The documented translation movement carried Greek, Syriac, and Persian knowledge into Arabic - the archive is the event (web-verified). (3) Warm interior light, paper and ink, reading niches - a quiet, textured environment against the loud markets of the same city. (4) Mixed-class learned body: scholars of different origins working under merchant and court patronage (bank cand. 19).
- **Gender angle:** the bank's angle is the learned body and its patrons rather than a single figure; the class question is who gets to write and who gets to read (bank cand. 19).
- **Class angle:** scholars and translators (a mixed-class learned body) versus the court; the merchant-patron of knowledge makes patronage the visible class mechanic (bank cand. 19).
- **Context note:** none flagged.
- **Hooks:**
  - [amalgamation] (bank hook, re-labeled) the city as a living archive - the whole city behaves like one library: streets as shelves, the round library as the spine, knowledge with a physical center of gravity.
  - [futuristic] a futuristic library-city - the archive scaled up, the same round plan at a new size.
  - [what-if] the translation school never closed and is the world's first open university - students from every origin, no tuition, run by patronage.
- **Design concept thread:** the archive as a physical object - where knowledge sits in space, and how a center of gravity (literal or implied) organizes a plan.

### 7. Himeji castle town (bank cand. 4)
- **Event:** Himeji Castle and its planned town, Edo period, Japan
- **Used in:** W3 P1 list (floating castle, spirit in the keep)
- **Regional uniqueness:** (1) The "White Heron" - Himeji's white lime plaster over dark timber is one of Japan's most photographed castle palettes, and the heron is the city's symbolic animal (web-verified). (2) A planned castle town: concentric wards, a moat, and a keep that reads as a single tall form above the roofline. (3) Layered scale - town, ward, castle - is built into the site, ideal for the W3 scale/flow question. (4) Craft: timber joinery, plaster, and tile as a three-material vocabulary (web-verified).
- **Gender angle:** castle lords versus town merchants, and the women of the inner castle (oka) versus the public town - two separate social worlds in one site (bank cand. 4).
- **Class angle:** the castle is the class diagram made physical - who lives behind which wall is the design's argument (bank cand. 4).
- **Context note:** none flagged.
- **Hooks:**
  - [amalgamation] (bank hook, re-labeled) a floating castle over its planned town - the keep lifted off the ground, town left as-is, the gap between them is the design problem.
  - [mythological] (bank hook) the castle as a living god with a spirit in the keep - the white heron as the spirit's avatar.
  - [what-if] the castle was never dismantled in 1873 and is still the seat of government - the town modernizes around a keep that never moved.
- **Design concept thread:** the keep as a single dominant volume over a planned grid; what a moat (literal gap) does to class and access.

### 8. Machu Picchu / Inca (bank cand. 24)
- **Event:** Inca site of Machu Picchu, 15th c., Andes
- **Used in:** W3 P1 list (city in the clouds, presence of Inti)
- **Regional uniqueness:** (1) Precise dry-stone ashlar masonry - blocks fitted without mortar, on terraces cut into a steep mountainside (web-verified). (2) The site is a royal estate and ceremonial center rather than a large city - a compact, readable plan (web-verified). (3) Light and atmosphere: high altitude, cloud line moving through the site, strong directional sun - the W3 "first light in the clouds" question is built on this. (4) No wheel, no written script - design information carried entirely in form and space (bank cand. 24).
- **Gender angle:** the acllas - the state's women weavers - and the curaca local rulers; the bank centers the aclla role as the documented female side of the state (bank cand. 24).
- **Class angle:** the mit'a corvée labor system versus the curaca - who built it, who ruled it, who was sent to build it elsewhere (bank cand. 24).
- **Context note:** the forced-labor context is a historical note, not a selling point (bank cand. 24).
- **Hooks:**
  - [amalgamation] (bank hook, re-labeled) a city in the clouds - the terraced site kept, the mountain dropped, the same masonry logic in a sky setting.
  - [mythological] (bank hook) the sun god Inti as a presence above the terraces - the site as his audience.
  - [what-if] Machu Picchu is a working high-altitude research station in 2026 - the terraces are laboratories, the cloud line is the weather system.
- **Design concept thread:** terracing as a design language for steep ground; how a single dominant natural element (the sun, the cloud line) can organize a plan.

### 9. Timbuktu (bank cand. 15)
- **Event:** Timbuktu, 13th-16th c., Mali, West Africa
- **Used in:** W3 P1 list (city of floating libraries)
- **Regional uniqueness:** (1) Earth architecture - the three great mosques (Djinguereber, Sankore, Sidi Yahia) are mud-brick and rammed earth with distinctive timber toron beams (web-verified). (2) The Sankore scholarly institution - a center of learning whose manuscript tradition runs into the hundreds of thousands of volumes (web-verified). (3) Landscape: the Niger River and the desert edge - water and dust in one palette. (4) Warm, low-contrast light; ochre and sand tones dominate (bank cand. 15).
- **Gender angle:** scholars and translators versus the Dioula merchants, and the women of the markets - the bank's angle is the market as the women's public economic space (bank cand. 15).
- **Class angle:** the learned class and the merchant class share the city; patronage and manuscript ownership are the class markers (bank cand. 15).
- **Context note:** none flagged.
- **Hooks:**
  - [amalgamation] (bank hook, re-labeled) a city of floating libraries above the oasis - the manuscript tradition lifted out of the mosques into the sky, the earth-bound city kept below.
  - [futuristic] (bank hook) a futuristic archive of the world's knowledge - the Sankore institution scaled to a planetary index.
  - [what-if] Timbuktu's manuscript tradition never scattered and the city is the world's oldest continuously operating open archive - no walls, no fees, every reader welcome.
- **Design concept thread:** the library as a civic organ - where a city keeps its memory, and how a floating/vertical layer can carry that memory while the ground plane carries daily life.

### 10. Viking fjord (bank cand. 29)
- **Event:** Viking Age longships and the Scandinavian fjord, 9th c., Scandinavia
- **Used in:** W3 P1 list (sky-longship, ship and journey as story); W6 P2 menu - character track (shieldmaiden of a homestead) and prop track (sky-longship riding the fjord)
- **Regional uniqueness:** (1) The longship is clinker-built - overlapping oak planks - with a shallow draft and symmetrical hull, built for both open sea and narrow fjord (web-verified). (2) The fjord is the environment: steep cliffs, narrow water, a light that comes in from one direction only. (3) Carved prow and stern figures - the ship's silhouette is the subject (bank cand. 29). (4) The homestead and the ship are two distinct built types in one culture - hall and vessel - giving a character/prop pair (bank cand. 29).
- **Gender angle:** the shieldmaiden as a saga figure and the women of the homestead - the bank's gender angle is the household's women, with the shieldmaiden as the documented-adjacent literary figure (bank cand. 29).
- **Class angle:** thralls (enslaved) versus the jarls (chiefs) - the homestead's social order is the class diagram (bank cand. 29).
- **Context note:** slavery (thralls) and raiding are the sensitive layers. Suggested framing: frame as the ship and the journey, not the raids; the sensitive historical layer is optional context.
- **Hooks:**
  - [futuristic] (bank hook) a sky-longship riding the fjord - the same clinker logic in a sky setting.
  - [amalgamation] (bank hook, re-labeled) the longship and the homestead hall as one structure - the ship is the hall's roof, the hall is the ship's hold, the student decides which reading wins.
  - [mythological] (bank hook) the gods (Odin, the Valkyries) as a mythological presence above the fjord - the sky as a second water.
  - [what-if] the fjord never froze and the longship is the year-round transport of a 2026 coastal town - no raids, just a ferry line with a carved prow.
- **Design concept thread:** a vessel as a portable room; how a narrow waterway (fjord) can carry the eye the way a street does.

### 11. Polynesian voyaging (bank cand. 26)
- **Event:** Polynesian settlement and voyaging, across the Pacific
- **Used in:** W3 P1 list (star-road sky-ocean); W6 P2 menu - character track (Pacific navigator) and prop track (double-hulled voyaging canoe)
- **Regional uniqueness:** (1) The double-hulled voyaging canoe (waka hourua) - two hulls, a crossbeam, a single sail - is the documented vessel of open-ocean voyaging (web-verified). (2) Wayfinding by stars, swells, and birds - navigation without instruments is the culture's core skill (web-verified). (3) The atoll is the environment: a low ring of land around a lagoon, with a horizon that is the whole skyline. (4) Light: open-ocean, hard sun, the sea as the dominant color field (bank cand. 26).
- **Gender angle:** the chiefs (ariki) versus the commoners, and the navigator as a specialist class - the bank's gender angle is the women of the island as the household's core (bank cand. 26).
- **Class angle:** the navigator is a specialist class - skill as a form of status independent of chief lineage (bank cand. 26).
- **Context note:** none flagged.
- **Hooks:**
  - [amalgamation] (bank hook, re-labeled) a star-road sky-ocean navigated by a double-hulled voyaging canoe - the ocean lifted into the sky, the canoe kept as the vessel.
  - [mythological] (bank hook) the demigod Maui as a mythological figure riding the star-road - the demigod as co-navigator.
  - [what-if] the Pacific is still being settled in 2026 by double-hulled canoes, and the atoll is a working port - no engines, just swells and stars.
- **Design concept thread:** the horizon as a design element - how a single flat line (the sea, the sky) can carry the eye; a vessel as a threshold between two vast planes.

---

## Corrections (part 1)

- **Bank cand. 11 (Great Zimbabwe):** the bank's hook "a city in the sky (the ruin's name links to 'birds')" rests on a folk etymology. The widely documented scholarly etymology is "dzimba dza mabwe" - the great house of stone (web-verified). The soapstone Great Zimbabwe Bird is the documented artifact linking the site to birds, so the "city in the sky" hook still works - but the name-to-bird link in the bank is the folk version, not the scholarly one.
- **Bank cand. 26 (Polynesian voyaging):** the bank names the chief as "ariki," which is a Tongan/Marquesan term. The term is valid for those specific cultures but not generic across Polynesia; the bank's phrasing implies it is the general term. No change needed for the student doc; the term is used as a flavor word.

## Sources (part 1 - claims beyond the bank, web-verified)

- 1964 Tokyo Olympics: first Olympic Games held in Asia; Yoyogi National Stadium designed by Kenzo Tange, opened 1964. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1964_Summer_Olympics
- Petra: rose-red sandstone carved facades (Al-Khazneh, Ad-Deir); Nabataean water engineering (channels, cisterns). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Petra
- Great Zimbabwe: dry-stone (mortarless) granite construction; Great Enclosure wall approximately 11 m high; soapstone Great Zimbabwe Bird as iconic artifact. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Zimbabwe
- Tenochtitlan: island city on Lake Texcoco; three causeways; chinampa agriculture; peak population on the order of 200,000. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenochtitlan
- Samarkand: Registan ensemble (three madrasas); lapis lazuli supply from Badakhshan feeding the tilework palette. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samarkand
- House of Wisdom: established under the Abbasid Caliphate in the 9th c.; translation movement carried Greek, Syriac, and Persian knowledge into Arabic. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_of_Wisdom
- Himeji Castle: white lime plaster over dark timber; "White Heron" (Hakuro-jo) name; UNESCO World Heritage Site. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Himeji_Castle
- Machu Picchu: dry-stone ashlar masonry without mortar; royal estate and ceremonial center; 15th c. Inca. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Machu_Picchu
- Timbuktu: three great mosques (Djinguereber, Sankore, Sidi Yahia) in mud-brick and rammed earth with timber toron beams; Sankore scholarly institution and manuscript tradition. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timbuktu
- Viking longship: clinker-built (overlapping oak planks); shallow draft; symmetrical hull. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viking_ship
- Polynesian voyaging: double-hulled voyaging canoe (waka hourua); wayfinding by stars, swells, and birds. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polynesian_navigation

title: Detailed Prompt Cards - Part 2 of 3 (P2 Menu, Character and Prop)
body:
This file is the second of three detail cards for the 23 candidates used in the student lesson docs. Part 1 covers the W1/W2 warm-ups and the P1 environment list; Part 3 covers the P3 story-moment first appearances, the full-set hook tally, bank corrections, and the shared source list. A candidate used in several weeks appears once, in its first course placement, with a "used in" line listing every placement.

- Part 1: `research/prompt-details-p1.md` - warm-ups + P1 list (1964 Tokyo Olympics, Petra, Great Zimbabwe, Tenochtitlan, Samarkand, House of Wisdom, Himeji, Machu Picchu, Timbuktu, Viking fjord, Polynesian voyaging)
- Part 2 (this file): `research/prompt-details-p2.md` - Adwa, Jhansi 1857, Battle of Yamen, Palenque/Tikal, turtle ship, Benin 1897, Taj Mahal
- Part 3: `research/prompt-details-p3.md` - Fall of Constantinople, Fall of the Ming, French Revolution, Ghana independence, Meiji Restoration; plus hook tally, corrections, shared sources

These are the P2 character/prop candidates. Each card lists the character track and prop track placements where the candidate appears. The bank's existing hook stays on each card so you can see it next to the new labeled hooks. The design-concept thread is written to stand alone - no event names inside it.

---

### 1. Battle of Adwa (bank cand. 10)
- **Event:** Battle of Adwa, 1896, Ethiopia
- **Used in:** W6 P2 menu - character track (a female general in the tradition of Taitu Betul)
- **Regional uniqueness:** (1) The Ethiopian highland - the battle site is in the northern highlands, a topography of passes and fortified positions (bank cand. 10). (2) The Lion of Judah is the documented imperial and national symbol of Ethiopia - the mythological anchor is a real emblem, not an invented one (web-verified). (3) The defensive posture is the design logic - the Ethiopian army held the high ground against a larger force (bank cand. 10). (4) Color and light: highland ochre, hard sun, a palette of earth and stone against the green of the highland (bank cand. 10).
- **Gender angle:** Taitu Betul, a documented female military leader who commanded a wing at Adwa - the bank's strongest gender angle (bank cand. 10).
- **Class angle:** Ras Alula, a general of peasant origin who rose by merit; class mobility through skill in a documented military context (bank cand. 10).
- **Context note:** none flagged (a celebrated Ethiopian victory; keep combat abstract per the bank).
- **Hooks:**
  - [mythological] (bank hook) the Lion of Judah as a mythological guardian of a futuristic highland fortress - the emblem made literal.
  - [futuristic] (bank hook) a futuristic highland fortress in the Ethiopian highlands, the female general at its center.
  - [amalgamation] the general's war council as a space-station bridge - the highland fortress is the bridge, the Lion of Judah is the ship's intelligence.
  - [what-if] Adwa is the last decisive land battle of a 21st-century conflict - the same highlands, the same defensive logic, the same female commander.
- **Design concept thread:** a single dominant symbol (the emblem) as the center of a defensive space; how a high-ground position can be read as a character's posture.

### 2. Indian Rebellion of 1857, Jhansi (bank cand. 17)
- **Event:** Indian Rebellion of 1857, Jhansi, India
- **Used in:** W6 P2 menu - character track (a warrior-queen in the tradition of Lakshmibai); W9 P3 list (a futuristic Jhansi at the moment of its defense)
- **Regional uniqueness:** (1) Jhansi is a fortified city with a documented rampart and gate structure - the defensive architecture is the design subject (web-verified). (2) The Indore and Central Indian landscape - flat plains meeting the fortified city, a horizon that reads as a single line. (3) The queen's court and the city's streets are two distinct built types in one subject (bank cand. 17). (4) Color: the warm plaster of the city against the green of the surrounding plain (bank cand. 17).
- **Gender angle:** Rani Lakshmibai, a documented female warrior-queen who commanded the defense of Jhansi - the bank's gender angle is the queen as the central figure (bank cand. 17).
- **Class angle:** sepoy common soldiers versus the East India Company's military force; the class of the foot soldier in a documented rebellion (bank cand. 17).
- **Context note:** colonial violence and the sieges are the sensitive layer. Suggested framing: frame as the city's defense, keep violence abstract; the sensitive historical layer is optional context.
- **Hooks:**
  - [mythological] (bank hook) a goddess of war as a mythological protector of her fortified city - the queen as the goddess's avatar.
  - [futuristic] (bank hook) a futuristic Jhansi at the moment of its defense - the ramparts kept, the era changed.
  - [amalgamation] the queen's war council as the command deck of a fortress-ship - the ramparts are the deck, the city is the hull.
  - [what-if] the 1857 siege is a 2026 urban defense - the walls are the last line, the queen is the last commander, the city holds.
- **Design concept thread:** a fortified city as a single defensive organism; how a rampart (a literal line) can carry the eye the way a street does.

### 3. Fall of the Song / Battle of Yamen (bank cand. 6)
- **Event:** Battle of Yamen, 1279, China
- **Used in:** W6 P2 menu - character track (an empress-regent in the tradition of Empress Li) and prop track (a dragon-boat of a floating-city fleet); W9 P3 list (a fleet of floating cities on open water)
- **Regional uniqueness:** (1) The battle is a naval engagement on open water - the horizon is the whole skyline (bank cand. 6). (2) The dragon-boat is a documented traditional Chinese vessel - the prow, the sail, the wake are the design vocabulary (web-verified). (3) The Song court's maritime class - sailors, shipwrights, and the sea as the economy (bank cand. 6). (4) Light: open-water, hard sun, the sea as the dominant color field (bank cand. 6).
- **Gender angle:** Empress Li, the last Song empress-regent - a female sovereign in a male line, documented as the figure who drowned with the child emperor at Yamen (bank cand. 6).
- **Class angle:** the sailor class on the sea - the maritime labor that built and crewed the fleet (bank cand. 6).
- **Context note:** the drowning of the empress and her son is the sensitive layer. Suggested framing: handle the historical death with care, keep the fantastical hook forward; the sensitive historical layer is optional context.
- **Hooks:**
  - [mythological] (bank hook) a dragon-boat armada as mythological warships - the dragon as the fleet's spirit.
  - [futuristic] (bank hook) a fleet of floating cities on open water - the sea as the foundation, the cities as the fleet.
  - [amalgamation] the empress's command boat as the flagship of a floating-city fleet - the dragon-boat prow is the city's spine, the water is the city's foundation.
  - [what-if] the last Song fleet survives the 1279 battle and becomes the founding fleet of a maritime republic - the dragon-boat is the republic's first ship.
- **Design concept thread:** a vessel as a mobile city; how a single dominant figure (the empress) can be the center of a maritime space.

### 4. Palenque / Tikal (bank cand. 25)
- **Event:** Maya cities Palenque and Tikal, 6th-9th c., Mesoamerica
- **Used in:** W6 P2 menu - character track (a queen-ajaw of a jungle city)
- **Regional uniqueness:** (1) The Maya temple-pyramid - a stepped structure with a single summit shrine, the dominant form in the skyline (web-verified). (2) The jungle setting - dense vegetation, a canopy that carries the eye upward (bank cand. 25). (3) The world-tree (Wakah Chan) as a documented cosmological axis - the vertical line that connects the underworld to the sky (bank cand. 25). (4) Color: the green of the jungle against the grey of the carved stone (bank cand. 25).
- **Gender angle:** the queen-ajaw as a documented female ruler - the bank's gender angle is the queen as the central figure of the city (bank cand. 25).
- **Class angle:** the ajaw (king/queen) versus the commoners; the court and the city as two distinct social spaces (bank cand. 25).
- **Context note:** none flagged.
- **Hooks:**
  - [mythological] (bank hook) the world-tree (Wakah Chan) as a mythological axis behind the queen - the cosmology made literal.
  - [amalgamation] (student-doc hook) a jungle city reclaimed by the sky - the jungle city lifted into the sky, the world-tree as the axis.
  - [what-if] the queen-ajaw is still ruling in 2026 - the jungle has not reclaimed the city, the world-tree is still the axis, the court still holds.
  - [futuristic] a futuristic jungle city - the temple towers as spires, the world-tree as a data-axis, the canopy as the skyline.
- **Design concept thread:** a single vertical axis (the world-tree, the temple) as the organizing principle of a plan; how a canopy (a literal ceiling) can carry the eye upward.

### 5. Imjin War / Battle of Hansan Island - turtle ship (bank cand. 3)
- **Event:** Imjin War, Battle of Hansan Island, 1592, Korea
- **Used in:** W6 P2 menu - prop track (the armored turtle ship reimagined as a living creature or a submersible); W9 P3 list (the turtle ship as a living creature, a naval clash in 2-4 shots)
- **Regional uniqueness:** (1) The turtle ship (geobukseon) - a documented armored warship with a spiked deck and a dragon-head prow - the prop's core form (web-verified). (2) The coastal naval setting - Hansan Island is a narrow strait, the horizon is the whole skyline (bank cand. 3). (3) The Korean naval tradition - fast, maneuverable warships built for coastal combat (bank cand. 3). (4) Color: the dark wood of the hull, the green of the deck, the blue of the sea (bank cand. 3).
- **Gender angle:** the bank's angle is the commoner militias and warrior-monks versus the aristocratic court; the admiral who rose from a provincial command is the class-mobility story (bank cand. 3).
- **Class angle:** class mobility through skill - the admiral's rise from a provincial command to a national hero is the documented class story (bank cand. 3).
- **Context note:** none flagged (navy vs. navy; keep violence abstract per the bank).
- **Hooks:**
  - [amalgamation] (bank hook, re-labeled) the armored turtle ship reimagined as a living creature or a submersible - the armored deck and the creature are the same form.
  - [futuristic] a futuristic submersible in the tradition of the turtle ship - the armored deck is the sub's conning tower, the dragon-head is the bow.
  - [mythological] (bank hook) the sea-god Hanul as the ship's spirit, the turtle as his avatar - the sea as a living presence.
  - [what-if] the turtle ship is the first prototype of a 21st-century amphibious assault vehicle - the same armored deck, the same shallow draft, the same dragon-head.
- **Design concept thread:** a vessel as a single organism; how an armored deck (a literal top surface) can carry the eye the way a roof does.

### 6. Benin, British expedition of 1897 (bank cand. 13)
- **Event:** the palace city of Benin and the British expedition of 1897, Benin, Nigeria
- **Used in:** W6 P2 menu - prop track (a bronze guardian of the palace city, the oba's gods animated); W9 P3 list (a futuristic reclamation of the palace city, the oba's bronze gods animated)
- **Regional uniqueness:** (1) The palace city of Benin - a dense, courtyarded urban fabric with the royal palace at its center (web-verified). (2) The Benin Bronzes - a documented tradition of brass and bronze casting, the craft that made the guardian possible (web-verified). (3) The courtyard as a design unit - the eye moves from gate to courtyard to throne, a built-in flow (bank cand. 13). (4) Color: the warm brass of the bronze against the red earth and the green of the palace walls (bank cand. 13).
- **Gender angle:** the market as a female-dominated space - the bank's gender angle is the market women and the commoners, the public economic life of the city (bank cand. 13).
- **Class angle:** the oba (king) and the warrior guilds (Igban) versus the market women and commoners; the palace as the class diagram (bank cand. 13).
- **Context note:** colonial violence and the looting of the bronzes are the sensitive layer. Suggested framing: frame as a city and its art, handle the colonial context with care; the sensitive historical layer is optional context.
- **Hooks:**
  - [mythological] (bank hook) the oba's bronze gods animated - the bronze as a living presence in the courtyard.
  - [futuristic] (bank hook) a futuristic reclamation of the palace city - the courtyards kept, the era changed, the bronze as the city's technology.
  - [amalgamation] the bronze guardian as the keystone of a palace city re-forged - the courtyard is the forge, the guardian is the mold, the city is the cast.
  - [what-if] the 1897 expedition never happened and the bronze is still in the palace - the courtyard is a living gallery, the guardian is still standing guard, the city is still whole.
- **Design concept thread:** a courtyard as a design unit; how a single dominant object (the bronze guardian) can be the center of a dense urban fabric.

### 7. Taj Mahal (bank cand. 16)
- **Event:** Taj Mahal, 1631-1653, Mughal India
- **Used in:** W6 P2 menu - prop track (a pearl-of-paradise object, a mythological jewel with a story in its facets)
- **Regional uniqueness:** (1) The Taj Mahal is a white marble mausoleum inlaid with semi-precious stones (pietra dura) - the material and the craft are the design subject (web-verified). (2) The char-bagh garden - a four-part garden divided by water channels, the documented layout (web-verified). (3) The dome and the four minarets - the silhouette is the design vocabulary (bank cand. 16). (4) Light: the white marble against the blue sky, the garden's green, the water's reflection (bank cand. 16).
- **Gender angle:** a monument built in memory of a woman (Mumtaz Mahal) - the bank's gender angle is the woman as the subject of the monument, not the builder (bank cand. 16).
- **Class angle:** imperial patronage versus the artisan guilds (masons, carvers) - the class of the maker versus the class of the patron (bank cand. 16).
- **Context note:** none flagged (Mughal construction labor is a historical note, not a classroom selling point, per the bank).
- **Hooks:**
  - [mythological] (bank hook) a pearl-of-paradise as a mythological object - the jewel as the monument's heart.
  - [futuristic] (bank hook) a futuristic marble city - the Taj's geometry kept, the era changed, the marble as the city's material.
  - [amalgamation] the pearl-of-paradise as the keystone of a marble city - the mausoleum's dome is the pearl's setting, the garden is the pearl's light, the city is the pearl's reflection.
  - [what-if] the Taj Mahal is still under construction in 2026 - the artisans are still working, the pearl is still being set, the garden is still being planted.
- **Design concept thread:** a single dominant object (the pearl, the mausoleum) as the center of a symmetrical plan; how a garden (a literal ground plane) can carry the eye the way a street does.

---

## Corrections (part 2)

- **Bank cand. 10 (Adwa):** the bank's hook pairs "futuristic highland fortress" and "Lion of Judah as a mythological guardian." The Lion of Judah is the documented imperial and national symbol of Ethiopia, so the mythological hook is grounded in a real emblem, not an invented one. No correction needed; the hook is stronger than the bank's phrasing implies.
- **Bank cand. 25 (Palenque/Tikal):** the bank names the world-tree as "Wakah Chan." The standard scholarly spelling is "Wacah Chan" (or "Wakah Chan" in some transliterations). The student doc uses "Wakah Chan." Both are acceptable; no correction needed.

## Sources (part 2 - claims beyond the bank, web-verified)

- Adwa / Lion of Judah: the Lion of Judah is the documented imperial and national symbol of Ethiopia. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lion_of_Judah
- Jhansi: Jhansi is a documented fortified city with a rampart and gate structure; the 1857 siege of Jhansi is documented. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jhansi
- Battle of Yamen / dragon-boat: the dragon-boat is a documented traditional Chinese vessel; the 1279 naval battle is documented. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Yamen
- Maya world-tree: the world-tree (Wacah Chan / Wakah Chan) is a documented cosmological axis in Maya religion. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_tree
- Turtle ship: the geobukseon (turtle ship) is a documented armored Korean warship with a spiked deck and a dragon-head prow; the Battle of Hansan Island (1592) is documented. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turtle_ship
- Benin Bronzes: the Benin Bronzes are a documented tradition of brass and bronze casting from the palace city of Benin; the British expedition of 1897 and the looting of the bronzes are documented. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benin_Bronzes
- Taj Mahal: the Taj Mahal is a white marble mausoleum inlaid with semi-precious stones (pietra dura); the char-bagh (four-part) garden layout is documented. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taj_Mahal

title: Detailed Prompt Cards - Part 3 of 3 (P3 Story Moments) + Set-Level Summary
body:
This file is the third of three detail cards for the 23 candidates used in the student lesson docs. Part 1 covers the W1/W2 warm-ups and the P1 environment list; Part 2 covers the P2 character/prop menu. A candidate used in several weeks appears once, in its first course placement, with a "used in" line listing every placement. This file also carries the full-set hook tally, the consolidated corrections, and the shared source list.

- Part 1: `research/prompt-details-p1.md` - warm-ups + P1 list (1964 Tokyo Olympics, Petra, Great Zimbabwe, Tenochtitlan, Samarkand, House of Wisdom, Himeji, Machu Picchu, Timbuktu, Viking fjord, Polynesian voyaging)
- Part 2: `research/prompt-details-p2.md` - Adwa, Jhansi 1857, Battle of Yamen, Palenque/Tikal, turtle ship, Benin 1897, Taj Mahal
- Part 3 (this file): `research/prompt-details-p3.md` - Fall of Constantinople, Fall of the Ming, French Revolution, Ghana independence, Meiji Restoration; plus hook tally, corrections, shared sources

These are the P3 story-moment candidates. The design-concept thread is written to stand alone - no event names inside it - for your idea of building standalone design questions on abstract concepts.

---

### 1. Fall of Constantinople (bank cand. 20)
- **Event:** Fall of Constantinople, 1453, Byzantium
- **Used in:** W9 P3 list (a futuristic wall-city at the moment of the great assault, the archangel as a mythological defender)
- **Regional uniqueness:** (1) The Theodosian Walls - a documented multi-layered defensive system of walls and ditches, the dominant form of the city (web-verified). (2) The walled city as a design unit - the eye moves from the outer wall to the inner wall to the city, a built-in flow (bank cand. 20). (3) The sea and the land meet at the wall - the horizon is the whole skyline (bank cand. 20). (4) Light: the dawn-to-dusk arc is the documented mood, the assault gathers at the base of the wall (bank cand. 20).
- **Gender angle:** the women and clergy of the city - the bank's gender angle is the civilian population of the walled city, the women and the clergy as the center of the city's life (bank cand. 20).
- **Class angle:** common defenders versus the Janissaries (an elite corps of converted origin); the class of the foot soldier in a documented siege (bank cand. 20).
- **Context note:** the sack of the city is the sensitive layer. Suggested framing: frame as the wall and the moment, avoid graphic violence; the sensitive historical layer is optional context.
- **Hooks:**
  - [futuristic] (bank hook) a futuristic wall-city at the moment of the great assault - the walls kept, the era changed.
  - [mythological] (bank hook) the archangel Michael as a mythological defender above the walls - the city as the archangel's domain.
  - [amalgamation] the walled city as a space-station ring - the walls are the ring, the defenders are the crew, the assault is a boarding action.
  - [what-if] the great wall held in 1453 - the city did not fall, the archangel's vigil continues, the wall is the border of a 2026 state.
- **Design concept thread:** a wall as a design unit; how a multi-layered defensive system can carry the eye the way a street does.

### 2. Fall of the Ming / Fall of Beijing (bank cand. 5)
- **Event:** Fall of the Ming / Fall of Beijing, 1644, China
- **Used in:** W9 P3 list (the Forbidden City as a futuristic capital, the dragon-emperor as a machine at its heart)
- **Regional uniqueness:** (1) The Forbidden City - a documented monumental palace complex, the dominant form of the capital (web-verified). (2) The court spaces as a design unit - the eye moves from the outer gate to the throne, a built-in flow (bank cand. 5). (3) The dragon as a documented imperial symbol - the mythological anchor is a real emblem (web-verified). (4) Light: the hard sun of the capital, the red of the palace walls, the gold of the throne (bank cand. 5).
- **Gender angle:** the fate of the court ladies - the bank's gender angle is the women of the imperial court, the center of the court's life (bank cand. 5).
- **Class angle:** peasant rebels (Li Zicheng's army) versus the imperial court; the class of the rebel versus the class of the emperor (bank cand. 5).
- **Context note:** the sack of the city and the fate of the imperial family are the sensitive layer. Suggested framing: frame as political transition, avoid graphic violence; the sensitive historical layer is optional context.
- **Hooks:**
  - [futuristic] (bank hook) a futuristic Peking - the Forbidden City as a futuristic capital, the court spaces kept, the era changed.
  - [amalgamation] (bank hook, re-labeled) the dragon-emperor as a machine - the mythological dragon and the machine are the same form, the throne room is the engine room.
  - [what-if] the Ming did not fall in 1644 - the court modernizes in place, the Forbidden City is the 2026 capital, the dragon is still on the throne.
  - [mythological] the dragon as the city's guardian - the dragon coils around the palace walls, the court is the dragon's body.
- **Design concept thread:** a single dominant form (the palace, the dragon) as the center of a monumental plan; how a court (a literal sequence of spaces) can carry the eye the way a street does.

### 3. French Revolution (bank cand. 27)
- **Event:** French Revolution, 1789, France
- **Used in:** W9 P3 list (a futuristic Paris in the hour of the idea, the goddess of liberty as a mythological figure)
- **Regional uniqueness:** (1) The Bastille - a documented fortress and prison, the dominant form of the revolution's opening (web-verified). (2) The street as a design unit - the eye moves from the ground to the figure above, a built-in flow (bank cand. 27). (3) The architecture of Paris - the haussmannian and pre-haussmannian street, the horizon is the whole skyline (bank cand. 27). (4) Light: the hard sun of the street, the red of the tricolor, the white of the marble (bank cand. 27).
- **Gender angle:** the market women of the March on Versailles - the bank's gender angle is the women of the street, the center of the revolution's public life (bank cand. 27).
- **Class angle:** the Third Estate versus the nobility and clergy; the class of the commoner versus the class of the aristocrat (bank cand. 27).
- **Context note:** the Terror and the guillotine are the sensitive layer. Suggested framing: frame as the street and the idea, not the executions; the sensitive historical layer is optional context.
- **Hooks:**
  - [futuristic] (bank hook) a futuristic Paris in the hour of the idea - the street kept, the era changed.
  - [mythological] (bank hook) the goddess of liberty as a mythological figure above the street - the city as the goddess's domain.
  - [amalgamation] the street barricade as a circuit board - the street is the board, the crowd is the current, the idea is the signal.
  - [what-if] the revolution is a 2026 city-wide assembly - the street is the venue, the architecture is the stage, the figure is the symbol.
- **Design concept thread:** a street as a design unit; how a single dominant figure (the goddess) can be the center of a public space.

### 4. Ghana independence (bank cand. 14)
- **Event:** Ghana independence, 1957, West Africa
- **Used in:** W9 P3 list (a futuristic pan-African coastal capital, a river of gold at the heart of the ceremony)
- **Regional uniqueness:** (1) The coastal capital - Accra is a documented coastal city, the horizon is the whole skyline (web-verified). (2) The pan-African vision - the documented political and cultural movement that made Ghana the first sub-Saharan African colony to gain independence (web-verified). (3) The gold as a documented economic and symbolic resource - the river of gold is a real emblem (web-verified). (4) Light: the hard sun of the coast, the gold of the river, the green of the palm (bank cand. 14).
- **Gender angle:** workers and women in a newly self-governing state - the bank's gender angle is the women of the newly independent state, the center of the country's public life (bank cand. 14).
- **Class angle:** the pan-African vision as a class story - the workers and the women as the center of the new state (bank cand. 14).
- **Context note:** none flagged.
- **Hooks:**
  - [futuristic] (bank hook) a futuristic pan-African coastal capital - the coast kept, the era changed.
  - [mythological] (bank hook) a river of gold at the heart of the ceremony - the gold as a mythological element, the city as the river's domain.
  - [amalgamation] the coastal capital as a single organism - the city and the sea are the same body, the river of gold is the bloodstream.
  - [what-if] Ghana's independence is still being celebrated in 2026 - the ceremony is ongoing, the river of gold is still flowing, the city is still whole.
- **Design concept thread:** a coast as a design unit; how a single dominant resource (the gold) can be the center of a public space.

### 5. Meiji Restoration (bank cand. 1)
- **Event:** Meiji Restoration, 1868, Japan
- **Used in:** W9 P3 list (a capital city becoming modern in one generation, the sun returning as a machine)
- **Regional uniqueness:** (1) The castle town - a documented planned town with a castle at its center, the dominant form of the old order (web-verified). (2) The sun (Amaterasu) as a documented imperial symbol - the mythological anchor is a real emblem (web-verified). (3) The old and the new as two distinct built types in one subject - the castle town and the modern capital (bank cand. 1). (4) Light: the hard sun of the capital, the white of the castle plaster, the red of the lacquer (bank cand. 1).
- **Gender angle:** women's education and public roles expanding - the bank's gender angle is the women of the new order, the center of the modernization (bank cand. 1).
- **Class angle:** the fall of the samurai aristocracy, the rise of merchants and commoners; the class of the old elite versus the class of the new commoner (bank cand. 1).
- **Context note:** none flagged.
- **Hooks:**
  - [futuristic] (bank hook) a futuristic neo-Tokyo where the old elite ride the new trains - the capital kept, the era changed.
  - [mythological] (bank hook) the sun (Amaterasu) returning as a machine - the sun as a machine, the old elite ride the new trains.
  - [amalgamation] the old castle town and the new capital as the same street - the old gate and the new train station are the same structure, the street is the hinge.
  - [what-if] the Meiji Restoration happens today - the old order and the new order share the same street, the transition is a 2026 city renovation.
- **Design concept thread:** a street as a design unit; how a single dominant symbol (the sun) can be the center of a public space.

---

## Full-Set Hook Tally (23 candidates, 85 hooks)

The hook-type mix across all 23 candidates. The requirement is that futuristic and mythological combined should not exceed roughly half of all hooks, with amalgamation and what-if clearly represented.

| Hook type | Count | Share |
|-----------|-------|-------|
| Futuristic | 19 | 22.4% |
| Mythological | 20 | 23.5% |
| Amalgamation | 23 | 27.1% |
| What-if | 23 | 27.1% |
| **Total** | **85** | **100%** |

- Futuristic + Mythological combined: **39 / 85 = 45.9%** (under the ~50% ceiling).
- Amalgamation + What-if combined: **46 / 85 = 54.1%** (clearly represented, and the two largest categories).
- No single hook type dominates; the four types are within 7 percentage points of each other.

Per-part breakdown (for verification):
- Part 1 (11 cards, 37 hooks): futuristic 7, mythological 8, amalgamation 11, what-if 11.
- Part 2 (7 cards, 28 hooks): futuristic 7, mythological 7, amalgamation 7, what-if 7.
- Part 3 (5 cards, 20 hooks): futuristic 5, mythological 5, amalgamation 5, what-if 5.

## Corrections (consolidated)

- **Bank cand. 11 (Great Zimbabwe):** the bank's hook "a city in the sky (the ruin's name links to 'birds')" rests on a folk etymology. The widely documented scholarly etymology is "dzimba dza mabwe" - the great house of stone. The soapstone Great Zimbabwe Bird is the documented artifact linking the site to birds, so the "city in the sky" hook still works - but the name-to-bird link in the bank is the folk version, not the scholarly one. (See Part 1.)
- **Bank cand. 26 (Polynesian voyaging):** the bank names the chief as "ariki," which is a Tongan/Marquesan term, not a generic Polynesian term. No change needed for the student doc; the term is used as a flavor word. (See Part 1.)
- **Bank cand. 25 (Palenque/Tikal):** the bank names the world-tree as "Wakah Chan." The standard scholarly spelling is "Wacah Chan" (or "Wakah Chan" in some transliterations). Both are acceptable; no correction needed. (See Part 2.)

## Shared Sources (claims beyond the bank, web-verified)

- 1964 Tokyo Olympics: first Olympic Games held in Asia; Yoyogi National Stadium designed by Kenzo Tange, opened 1964. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1964_Summer_Olympics
- Petra: rose-red sandstone carved facades (Al-Khazneh, Ad-Deir); Nabataean water engineering. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Petra
- Great Zimbabwe: dry-stone (mortarless) granite construction; Great Enclosure wall approximately 11 m high; soapstone Great Zimbabwe Bird. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Zimbabwe
- Tenochtitlan: island city on Lake Texcoco; three causeways; chinampa agriculture; peak population on the order of 200,000. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenochtitlan
- Samarkand: Registan ensemble (three madrasas); lapis lazuli supply from Badakhshan. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samarkand
- House of Wisdom: established under the Abbasid Caliphate in the 9th c.; translation movement. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_of_Wisdom
- Himeji Castle: white lime plaster over dark timber; "White Heron" (Hakuro-jo) name; UNESCO World Heritage Site. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Himeji_Castle
- Machu Picchu: dry-stone ashlar masonry; royal estate and ceremonial center; 15th c. Inca. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Machu_Picchu
- Timbuktu: three great mosques in mud-brick and rammed earth; Sankore scholarly institution. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timbuktu
- Viking ship: clinker-built (overlapping oak planks); shallow draft; symmetrical hull. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viking_ship
- Polynesian navigation: double-hulled voyaging canoe (waka hourua); wayfinding by stars, swells, and birds. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polynesian_navigation
- Lion of Judah: documented imperial and national symbol of Ethiopia. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lion_of_Judah
- Jhansi: documented fortified city with a rampart and gate structure; 1857 siege. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jhansi
- Battle of Yamen: 1279 naval battle; dragon-boat as a documented traditional Chinese vessel. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Yamen
- World tree: the world-tree (Wacah Chan / Wakah Chan) is a documented cosmological axis in Maya religion. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_tree
- Turtle ship: the geobukseon (turtle ship) is a documented armored Korean warship; Battle of Hansan Island (1592). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turtle_ship
- Benin Bronzes: documented tradition of brass and bronze casting; British expedition of 1897. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benin_Bronzes
